mainTopic: The ban on remarrying a wife divorced for a bad name or a vow: its reason, when it applies, and when it does not
overview: The amud asks why a man who divorced his wife because of a bad name (שם רע) or a vow (נדר) may not remarry her. In one version of רב נחמן's teaching, the reason is קלקולא: the fear that the husband will later attack the גט, so he should not state his reason. In another version, it is a penalty that warns Jewish women not to be careless with עריות and נדרים, so he must state it. The גמרא brings a ברייתא supporting each version: רבי מאיר for the first and רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי for the second. Next it explains רבי יהודה's view that only a vow known to רבים blocks remarriage, which he learns from the oath to the גבעונים. The רבנן reject that proof. רב נחמן and רבי יצחק then argue whether רבים means three or ten people. The גמרא then explains the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר over vows that need a חכם, which depends on whether a husband minds his wife being embarrassed in בית דין. Finally, it fills in a missing line in the משנה: if the husband made the vow, he may remarry her, as the story in צידן shows.

steps.title: First version: the worry is that he could ruin her later
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the first version of רב נחמן's teaching, which began just before this section. The reason he may not remarry her is קלקולא: if he states the reason, he can later ruin her divorce. If he does not state it, he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: The quoted words are 'Because of a vow I am removing you.' רב נחמן holds that the reason for the rule is the fear of harm. If he said this to her, he is able to harm her later. If he did not say it, he cannot harm her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the words the husband might say and explains the reasoning behind רב נחמן's first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband openly says 'I am divorcing you because of a vow,' he could later claim the whole divorce was based on that reason. If the reason turns out to be false, he might say the גט was a mistake. If he never said the reason, such a claim gets nowhere, so in this version he should keep quiet about it.

keyTerms.meaning: I am sending you out, meaning divorcing you
Ruin or harm, here meaning damage to the validity of her divorce

steps.confusionAlert: The 'harm' is not physical. It means he could later attack the validity of the גט, which would make her children from a second marriage ממזרים.

phrases.english: "Because of a vow I am sending you out."
He holds: what is the reason?
Because of the harm.
If he said this to her,
he is able to harm her,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – לָא מָצֵי מְקַלְקֵל לַהּ.
phrases.english: and if not, he is not able to harm her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first version of רב נחמן's teaching, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on remarrying her exists because of קלקולא. Stating the reason gives him a way to ruin the divorce, so he should not state it.

steps.title: Second version: he must tell her the reason
steps.stepSummary: A second version of רב נחמן's teaching says the husband MUST tell her he is divorcing her because of a bad name or a vow. In this version the rule is a penalty that teaches Jewish women not to be careless with עריות and נדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version. רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: He must say to her, 'Know that I am divorcing you because of a bad name, and because of a vow.' His reasoning is that the rule exists so Jewish women will not be loose in matters of forbidden relations and vows. Therefore he must say this to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of רב נחמן's teaching, which says the opposite: the husband must tell her the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ban on remarrying is a קנס (penalty) on the woman for her behavior. A penalty only teaches a lesson if people know about it. So he has to say the reason out loud, which also warns other women.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad name, a suspicion of improper behavior

steps.whyThisMatters: The two versions disagree about the reason for the rule, and that changes the practical instruction: say nothing, or say it out loud.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Nachman said:
He must say to her: "Know
that because of a bad name I am sending you out,
and because of a vow I am sending you out."
He holds: what is the reason?
So that Jewish women will not be
loose in forbidden relations and in vows.
Therefore he must say this to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of רב נחמן with a different reason and the opposite instruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He must tell her the reason, because the ban is a penalty meant to warn Jewish women about עריות and נדרים.

steps.title: Each version has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports the first version and another ברייתא supports the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא taught in line with the first version, and there is a ברייתא taught in line with the second version.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us it is about to bring sources backing each version, starting with the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not pick a winner here. It shows that both versions have support from earlier teachings. The sources themselves come in the next steps.

phrases.english: It was taught in line with the first version,
and it was taught in line with the latter version.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא, וְתַנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces sources supporting both versions just presented.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both versions of רב נחמן have support from a ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's ברייתא supports the worry about ruining the divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains why a man who divorced his wife for a bad name or a vow may not remarry her. Otherwise, if she remarries and the reason proves false, he might claim he never would have divorced her. That would cancel the גט and make her children ממזרים. So we warn him in advance that he can never take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא supporting the first version. רבי מאיר said: Why did the חכמים say that a man who divorces his wife because of a bad name may not take her back, and one who divorces her because of a vow may not take her back? Because perhaps she will go and marry another man, and the claims will turn out to be false. He will then say, 'Had I known it was so, even if they gave me a hundred מנה I would not have divorced her.' The גט would turn out to be void and her children ממזרים. Therefore we tell him: Know that one who divorces his wife because of a bad name may not take her back, and one who divorces because of a vow may not take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר, whose reasoning matches the first version: the rule exists to stop the husband from later ruining the divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's whole concern is that the husband might regret the divorce and challenge the גט, which is exactly קלקולא. Because he knows from the start that he can never remarry her, he divorces her with full awareness. Later he cannot claim he would not have divorced her had he known the truth.

keyTerms.meaning: He may not take her back (remarry her)
Children born from a forbidden union, such as a married woman with another man

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר supports the first version: the ban on remarrying exists to protect the woman and her future children from the husband later attacking the גט.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'we tell him' means warning the husband that he can never remarry her. That is a different act from the husband telling the wife his reason, which is what the two versions argued about.

phrases.english: It was taught in line with the first version:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said: For what reason did they say

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שֵׁם רַע לֹא יַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: that one who divorces his wife because of a bad name may not take her back,
and one who divorces her because of a vow may not take her back?
Perhaps she will go and marry another man,
and the claims will turn out to be false,
and he will say: "Had I known that it was so,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אִם הָיוּ נוֹתְנִים לִי מֵאָה מָנֶה –
phrases.english: even if they had given me a hundred maneh,
I would not have divorced her."
Then the divorce would turn out to be void, and her children mamzerim.
Therefore we say to him: Know

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שֵׁם רַע – לֹא יַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: that one who divorces his wife because of a bad name may not take her back,
and one who divorces because of a vow may not take her back.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא – אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the first promised ברייתא, the one supporting the first version.
steps.raayaObject: The first version of רב נחמן, which holds that the reason for the rule is קלקולא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי מאיר explaining that the ban prevents the husband from later voiding the גט and making her children ממזרים.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting the second version
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי teaches that the ban on remarrying is a penalty so women will not be careless with עריות and נדרים. Therefore the husband is told to state the reason for the divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא matches the second version. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said: Why did they say that a man who divorces his wife because of a bad name may not take her back, and because of a vow may not take her back? So that Jewish women will not be careless with forbidden relations and with vows. That is why we tell him: Say to her, 'Know that I am divorcing you because of a bad name,' or 'because of a vow.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second ברייתא promised in step 3. It supports the second version of רב נחמן's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, רבי מאיר's reason was to protect the גט from being ruined later. Here the reason is a penalty that warns other women. Because the goal is to warn people, the husband is told to say the reason out loud. That is exactly what the second version required.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter version (here, the second version of רב נחמן's teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the ban on remarrying. רבי מאיר's reason is to protect the גט, so the husband should NOT state the reason. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's reason is a penalty that warns women, so the husband MUST state the reason.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with the second version:
phrases.notes: This is the second version of רב נחמן from step 2, where the husband must tell her the reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei said:
For what reason did they say

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִשּׁוּם שֵׁם רַע לֹא יַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: that one who divorces his wife because of a bad name may not take her back,
and one who divorces her because of a vow may not take her back?
So that Jewish women will not be
careless with forbidden relations and with vows.
Therefore we say to him: Say to her:

phrases.aramaic: ״הָוֵי יוֹדַעַת שֶׁמִּשּׁוּם שֵׁם רַע אֲנִי מוֹצִיאֵךְ
phrases.english: 'Know that I am divorcing you because of a bad name,'
or 'I am divorcing you because of a vow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 4: step 4 supported the first version, and this step supports the second version.
steps.raayaObject: The second version of רב נחמן: the husband must state the reason for the divorce, and the rule is a penalty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only a vow known to many blocks remarriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה. If many people knew about the vow, the husband may not take her back. If many people did not know, he may take her back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Any vow that many people knew about, he may not take her back. A vow that many people did not know about, he may take her back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and quotes רבי יהודה's view. This sets up the next question: what is his reason?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not apply the ban on remarrying to every vow. The rule depends on whether רבים knew about the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: He may take her back (remarry her)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל נֶדֶר שֶׁיֵּדְעוּ בּוֹ רַבִּים – לֹא יַחְזִיר,
phrases.english: Any vow that many people knew about, he may not take her back;
and one that many people did not know about, he may take her back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, after finishing the two ברייתות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow known to רבים blocks remarriage. A vow not known to רבים does not.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks what the source is for רבי יהודה's difference between a public vow and a private one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks why it matters whether many people knew about the vow. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks for a source. Why should a vow known to many be treated differently from a private one?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for treating a public vow differently.

steps.title: The source: the oath to the גבעונים
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the פסוק about the גבעונים. בני ישראל did not strike them because the leaders had sworn to them, which shows that an oath made before many people stays in force.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the children of Israel did not strike them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers his own question with a פסוק from יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leaders swore publicly to the גבעונים, and that oath was kept even though it was made under a trick. This shows that an oath known to many is treated as unbreakable. In the same way, a vow known to רבים stays fixed, so the husband may not take her back.

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And the children of Israel did not strike them,
because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them.'
phrases.notes: יהושע 9:18. "Them" means the גבעונים, who tricked בני ישראל into a peace treaty.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The public oath to the גבעונים was kept, so a vow known to רבים cannot be undone.

steps.title: The רבנן reject the proof from the גבעונים
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the oath to the גבעונים never took effect at all, because it was made under a lie. בני ישראל spared them only to avoid a חילול השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? There, did the oath take effect on them at all? Since the גבעונים told them, 'We came from a far land,' and they had not, the oath never took effect. The reason they did not kill them was because of קדושת השם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the רבנן, who disagree with רבי יהודה, push away his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that the oath was binding because it was public. The רבנן answer that the oath was not binding at all, because it was based on a lie. So the story proves nothing about public vows. בני ישראל spared the גבעונים only so that people would not think they broke their word.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן agree that בני ישראל did not kill the גבעונים. They only disagree about WHY: in their view it was not because the oath was binding, but to protect קדושת השם.

phrases.english: And the רבנן (how do they answer this)?

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, מִי חָלָה שְׁבוּעָה עִילָּוַיְיהוּ כְּלָל?!
phrases.english: There, did the oath take effect on them at all?!
Since they said to them:
'We came from a far land' (יהושע 9:6), and they had not come from there,
the oath did not take effect on them at all;
and the fact that they did not kill them
was because of the sanctity of God's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן הָתָם מִי חָלָה שְׁבוּעָה עִילָּוַיְיהוּ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the גבעונים for רבי יהודה's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The oath was made under a lie and never took effect. Sparing the גבעונים was only to avoid a חילול השם.

steps.title: How many people count as many?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many people are needed to count as רבים for רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many people count as 'many'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of רבים. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule depends on whether רבים knew about the vow, so we need to know the minimum number of people.

phrases.english: And how many people are 'many'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's rule in step 6 to define its key term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum number of people that counts as רבים.

steps.title: Three or ten
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says three people count as many. רבי יצחק says ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said three. רבי יצחק said ten.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give different numbers for how many people count as רבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a dispute: for רב נחמן, three people are enough to make the vow 'public', while רבי יצחק requires ten.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: three;
Rabbi Yitzchak said: ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר עֲשָׂרָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן: three people. רבי יצחק: ten people.

steps.title: Where the numbers three and ten come from
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן learns 'three' from the words 'ימים רבים' said about a זבה. רבי יצחק learns 'ten' from the word 'עדה' in the story of the גבעונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said three: 'days' means two, and adding 'many' makes it three. רבי יצחק said ten, because the פסוק says 'congregation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for each of the two numbers from the last step. Each אמורא brings a word from a פסוק to back up his number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reasons that a plural word like 'days' already means at least two, so the extra word 'many' must mean at least three. רבי יצחק uses the פסוק about the גבעונים, which is already the source for the public-vow rule. That פסוק says the leaders of the 'עדה' swore, and an עדה is ten people.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Many days,' the words used for a זָבָה
Congregation, a group of at least ten people

steps.whyThisMatters: These sources set the smallest group that turns a private vow into a public one, which cannot be undone under רבי יהודה's rule.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: three,
"days" means two,
phrases.notes: From the פסוק about a זבה, 'ימים רבים' (ויקרא 15:25).

phrases.english: "many" makes it three.
Rabbi Yitzchak said: ten,
as it is written: "congregation."
phrases.notes: This is the גבעונים פסוק from step 8 (יהושע 9:18). An עדה is ten, like the spies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind each number stated in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The minimum number of people that counts as רבים
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 15:25 ('ימים רבים') for three; יהושע 9:18 ('נשיאי העדה') for ten

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains the reason behind רבי מאיר's rule differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר's line in the משנה, then brings a ברייתא. There רבי אלעזר says the ban on remarrying after a vow that needs a חכם exists only because of vows that do not need a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי מאיר says: any vow that requires a חכם, and so on.' A ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר says, they forbade the case of 'requires' only because of the case of 'does not require.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, רבי מאיר's opinion. It brings a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר gives a different picture of which case is the real worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says that if a man divorced his wife over a vow that needs a חכם to undo it, he may not remarry her. If the vow is one the husband himself could have cancelled, he may remarry her. רבי אלעזר turns this around. He says the real worry is the vow the husband could have cancelled, and the חכמים then extended the ban to vows that need a חכם too.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow that needs a חכם to look into it and undo it
'And so on,' short for the rest of the quoted line
They forbade it only because of

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying the ban on 'requires' is wrong. In his view both cases are forbidden, and the 'does not require' case is the main one. That is where he differs from רבי מאיר, who permits remarriage in the 'does not require' case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
any vow that requires, etc.:
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The full line is about a vow that requires a חכם to undo it.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
They did not forbid the case of "requires"
except because of the case that "does not require."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָסְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'how many is רבים' discussion and opens a new topic: רבי מאיר's line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, the ban on remarrying after a vow that needs a חכם is only an extension of the ban for vows that do not need a חכם.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what principle splits רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר. This question sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They really disagree in practice. For a vow the husband could have cancelled himself ('does not require'), רבי מאיר lets him remarry her, while רבי אלעזר forbids it, and even treats it as the main case. The גמרא wants the reasoning behind this split, not just the two rulings.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two views given in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle underlying the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר

steps.title: Does a husband mind his wife being embarrassed in court?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a man does not mind his wife being embarrassed in בית דין. רבי אלעזר holds that he does mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: a man is willing to have his wife embarrassed in בית דין. רבי אלעזר holds: a man is not willing to have his wife embarrassed in בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The dispute depends on whether a husband would agree to bring his wife to a חכם in בית דין to undo her vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the husband will later claim, 'Had I known, I would not have divorced her,' and this would spoil the גט. For רבי מאיר, he is believed when he says he would have taken her to a חכם, so vows that need a חכם are the worry. For רבי אלעזר, he would not take her to court, so that claim is not believed. He is believed, though, when he says he did not know he could cancel the vow himself, so that becomes the main worry.

keyTerms.meaning: A man is willing, does not mind
That she be embarrassed or disgraced
Court, here where a חכם would undo the vow

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the husband does not mind going to court, so vows needing a חכם are the main worry. רבי אלעזר: he does mind, so the real worry is vows he could have cancelled himself, and the ban was extended from there.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אדם רוצה' does not mean the husband wants his wife shamed. It means he does not mind it enough to avoid going to a חכם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
a man is willing,
that his wife be embarrassed in court;
and Rabbi Elazar holds:
a man is not willing
that his wife be embarrassed in court.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether a husband minds his wife being embarrassed in בית דין, which decides which of his later claims would be believed.

steps.title: Why does the משנה bring the story from צידן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's story in the משנה and asks how it connects to what came before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: There was a story in צידן, and so on. What did the משנה teach that leads him to tell this story?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the story at the end of the משנה and asks why it is there. The story does not seem to match the case the משנה was just discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had been discussing a woman's vow, which keeps her husband from remarrying her. The story is about a vow made by the husband, and it ends with him being allowed to remarry her. So the story seems to have nothing to illustrate.

keyTerms.meaning: A true story or incident brought to show how a law works
צידן, a town where this story took place
What did he teach that he now brings this? The גמרא is asking how something connects to what came before

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident in Tzaidan, etc.
What did the משנה teach that he tells this story?
phrases.notes: The problem: the משנה was talking about the wife's vow, and this story is about the husband's vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר to the last line of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The placement of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's story in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story should illustrate the law stated just before it. Here the law is about the wife's vow, but the story is about the husband's vow and allows remarriage.

steps.title: The משנה is missing a line about the husband's vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words. The ban applies when she vowed, but if he vowed he may remarry her, and the story from צידן shows this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing words, and this is what it means: When is this said? When she made the vow. But if he made the vow, he may take her back. And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: There was also a story in צידן about a man who said to his wife, 'קונם if I do not divorce you.' He divorced her, and the חכמים allowed him to remarry her, for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in a missing line in the משנה. Once that line is added, the story fits perfectly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added line limits the ban on remarrying to a case where the wife made the vow. If the husband made the vow, he may remarry her. The story from צידן is an example of exactly that kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing from the משנה, and the גמרא fills them in
When is this rule said? This introduces a limit on a rule
A word used to make a vow that forbids something
He may take her back, meaning remarry her
The betterment of the world, meaning keeping society in good order

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on remarrying is only when the wife vowed. When the husband vowed, he may remarry her, as the story in צידן shows.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the story as an exception that goes against the משנה. Once the missing line is filled in, the story is a direct example of the משנה's rule.

phrases.english: The משנה is missing words
and this is what it is teaching:
When is this said?
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule that he may not take her back after a vow.

phrases.english: When she made the vow,
but if he made the vow, he may take her back;
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was also an incident in Tzaidan,
with one man who said to his wife:
"Konam if I do not divorce you,"
phrases.notes: קונם is a vow word. He bound himself with a vow unless he divorced her.

phrases.english: and he divorced her,
and the Sages allowed him to remarry her
for the betterment of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the story appears in the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fills in missing words in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ban on remarrying seemed to cover every vow, which left the story about the husband's vow out of place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies only to the wife's vow. If the husband vowed, he may remarry her, as the story in צידן shows.
